dialect: Egyptian Arabic, Cairene colloquial, written in Arabic script without vowel marks (colloquial spelling conventions)

profile.grammar_notes: No present-tense copula (zero copula for identity and state); فيه for existence ('there is'); عند + pronoun suffix for possession ('have'); negation with ما...ش circumfix on verbs and مش for nominal/adjectival sentences and future; questions by intonation plus postposed question words (فين، إيه، إمتى، إزاي، ليه، مين); b- prefix marks habitual/progressive present, ح- (or هـ) marks future; كان for past state; modality via عايز (want), لازم (must), ممكن (can/possible), يقدر (be able); politeness via حضرتك rather than verb morphology. Closed sets: independent pronouns (أنا، إنت، إنتي، هو، هي، إحنا، إنتو، هم), possessive/object suffixes, question words, demonstratives (ده، دي، دول).
